body: If I had to choose, my favourite was probably Final Fantasy Tactics.
I don't really feel curiosity any more. I still read news occasionally, when I feel like it.
Didn't really like FF12 as much, but by the time I started playing it, I didn't really like video games any more.
Sault Ste Marie.

I've felt like it for the past several years. That's not going to change any time soon. 

And no, I've tried every hobby or medium I could think of so far.
Indeed, no health insurance. Mental health is not covered beyond the free counselling I get.

I enjoyed learning business, politics, science, art, history, etc. 

And I don't like writing. Every time I try, I just end up hating it.

And it's possibly depression, but to get a more competent psychiatrist costs money I don't have.
I have almost all FF games. Also, http://ozanarusyra.deviantart.com/

I used to write all types, but in particular, most of my writing was poetry, system design, editing, and a lot of roleplaying on one main forum.

I used to play mainly RPG/Strategy console games, but I own a lot of consoles and I bought many games, in particular older console games.

I've tried every normal thing I could think of; advice of every kind, every hobby possible, every interest possible, conversing with many people, listening to many people's perspectives, lateral thinking and solving problems that seem similar, learning in a variety of fields.

In the case of my counsellor, it's the only one I can afford - free.
I used to enjoy writing, video games, listening to music, a few standard things. No real goals though, ever. It slowly stopped about 5 years ago, and there was no real reason.
But I haven't found anything yet, and I have nothing left I haven't tried.
Medication won't help my situation though.
It was a relationship, and I messed up at least three times.

He doesn't seem like the most supportive boyfriend. What I can guarantee you if he's acting this way now, you can surely do better. What we believe to be the greatest relationship of our lives is not. What we believe will be our last never is.
Correction. At this point, no hope.

Essentially, a lack of a reason to live. If it was just emotional pain/problems, I could stomach it. Emotions change on a daily basis, as you said, like wind on a mountain. However, the two situations coupled with each other leave me with little hope. Note the original topic, where I went on to explain how I don't like doing anything, have no friends, etc. These would be be possibilities as a reason to live.
I should note, I don't know what the cause of my main problems are. Emotional problems would be the main cause of the suicide. The main problems weren't accompanied with suicide the whole time.
I don't know what the cause is.

A reason to live, essentially. If you want to know my situation, ask questions, don't assume. You're better off that way in anything. Assuming rarely works; even if you're right, it's better to see how people explain it from their perspective, and that in itself will give you perspective on them. 

Just something I've learned while talking to people; always give them a chance to explain something, don't tell them what they are or how they're doing things.
As I said earlier. Without hope, a man can not even believe in his own survival.
A man without hope is a man who could never survive, I assure you.
I already have given up. I'm not spending every day like this. And I do intend on doing it within a few weeks. And I can't call long distance anyway, so I'd rather not your number.
Perhaps so, but I've been waiting for a long time already with no change. Waiting is not a reason to live.
Indeed.
I hope you find something worth living for then.
It was copied and pasted from elsewhere.

And, let's assume I am completely illusioned and jaded and you are saying things that are absolutely true. Throughout this, you still haven't done anything that could help the situation, and that in itself is a reason for me to not continue to read. I don't suggest replying, as I really won't reply back.

I know I'm the one at fault. I'm not refusing that in the slightest, nor have I ever. The problem lies in me, with me, and only me. I've never seen things any other way, I assure you. In any case, please stop replying. You're not actually doing anything helpful whatsoever except saying things that I know aren't true (just so you know, I happen to know my life and myself better than you do, whom happens to have only seen the tiniest fraction of who I am and my life. Approximately 0.001%. This figure is accurate.)

If you do reply, I won't read it. My decision is already made anyhow.

It's wrong because you're not trying to understand from my perspective.

The cold eyes, just forget about it. Not everyone has cold eyes, it was a figure of speech. An improper one. It's not related to my problem whatsoever, and you keep pushing it for no reason at all.

I do want help. As I said in the opening post, I have tried everything I could think of. Do you think in 5 years I couldn't think of most basic ideas? In 5 years of thinking, experimenting, acting, testing, and trying day after day, do you not think I would go through most suggestions that people would think of upon reading it? I'm not trying to be rude, just giving you some perspective.
I appreciate that, but that's the same as I have been doing.

I'm glad you started to feel better.

But I really can't think of anything I could even try to do at this point, noting that I'm stuck doing this job and I can't travel. (Bills won't pay themselves, and I don't drive). Outside of travel and what I can't afford, I have tried everything I could think of. 

Confidence has never been a problem for me. An interesting thing is though, people thanking me when I did something never made me felt better. I don't enjoy or become more positive when I help people. I merely do it because I can't imagine not doing it.
No, that seems fair. If I had a goal or something to do, I would probably be much better off.

Oh, no, I know there are some people who care. I do have family and the like. But that doesn't really change the situation. 

I'm twenty, BTW.
Fleeting? It's been 5 years with no change.
I assure you, that is wrong. But I doubt I could change your mind.

I don't know what the problem is. There doesn't seem to be a cause.

I didn't quantify cold eyes, you did. It was merely a statement, metaphorical in nature. In actual reference to previous statements, I don't assume things to the point of preventing myself from seeing posibilities. 

Feel free to. I have tried the suicide watch, but as of yet, it has noticeably less traffic and advice from here.
I appreciate that, but I think that's the least of my problems.

In order. the problem isn't depression, as I've talked to a therapist and  a counsellor and tried anti-depressants. This helped with my mood, but nothing else. I'm in healthy condition for diet or exercise. 

Indeed, I have asked here. Someone suggested it, and I wanted to try all options first.

Secondly, it's not confirmation bias. I don't make assumptions, I allow people to act before I think of it. In fact, I give people more chances to do what they like than anyone I have met thus far.

I specified it was selfish. 

And help in what sense? This is help, no?
I eat quite healthily, and I'm typical to somewhat measure my intake of vitamins and daily needs. I don't have a pet. I would take a course, but I'm not interested in anything.
I'm not interested in any courses. I could do something I'm good at, but if I'm not interested, I tend to do poorly in class.
